segments.caption: Before the switch
segments.fact: NO MEAT · NO FISH · EGGS & DAIRY STAY

lines.text: What if everyone on Earth went vegetarian, overnight?
No meat, no fish. Just plants, eggs and dairy.
Day one. Butchers and burger bars open with nothing to sell.
Vegetable stalls are sold out by lunch.

segments.caption: Herds no longer needed
segments.fact: 80+ BILLION ANIMALS RAISED FOR MEAT A YEAR

lines.text: Week one. Every year, more than eighty billion land animals are raised for meat.
Now, none of them are needed, so farmers stop breeding them.
Month three. More than a billion people depend on livestock for a living.
Many could lose their income, especially herders on dry land where crops barely grow.
Year one. Livestock uses about eighty percent of the world's farmland, but gives us only seventeen percent of our calories.
Dairy cows and hens stay, but vast pastures fall quiet.
Year ten. Empty grazing land slowly turns back into forest and meadow, and wildlife returns.
By twenty fifty, researchers estimate a vegetarian world would cut food emissions by almost two thirds,
and prevent around seven million deaths a year through healthier eating.
A greener planet, but a hard switch for the people who farm animals.
So, would you give up meat to see it?
